content: Yes, that is correct. In many countries, including the United States, if you are switching health insurance providers at the start of a new year, you typically need to formally cancel your existing policy in writing by the end of the previous year (December 31st) to ensure the new policy takes effect on January 1st. This is to prevent gaps in coverage and to comply with insurance regulations. However, specific requirements can vary by insurer and region, so it's always best to confirm with your current insurer and the new insurer to ensure a smooth transition.
